key_insight: AI Buckingham autonomously identifies dominant dimensionless groups and regime-dependent scalings by combining LLM reasoning with symbolic and numerical tools.
engineering_relevance: For rough-wall turbulent drag modelling, it identifies informative reparameterizations of surface statistics that improve equivalent sand-grain roughness estimates.
method: Use LLM planning and literature retrieval to guide discovery and dimensional checks.
Identify physical regimes with gradient-based clustering and dominant dimensionless groups using mutual information.
Apply explicit numerical criteria to select group count and assess simplification.
evidence_signal: Across ten systems spanning fluid dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, thermal convection and additive manufacturing, the framework recovers established similarity representations and resolves regime-dependent scalings.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify prediction gains or establish generalization to unseen rough surfaces and flow conditions.
paper_title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
